rule.wall: the SAME wall rule as script/m14/cpp-dump-classify.ts, re-derived from the ANALYZER's own exported sets (not forked) so a rename fails here rather than misclassifying.
rule.disposition: RESOLVED = the rows moved into `resolved` by a measured mechanism · CLAIMED = an arbiter-verified claim in its own column, never a resolution · INSTRUMENT GAP = a fact EXISTS and the instrument cannot read it · RULED UNDECIDABLE = no fact can decide the rows, with a stated falsifier. Every wall lands in exactly one.

walls.disposition: SPLIT (see subs): the project-fact part is an INSTRUMENT GAP priced by the four-bucket partition; the receiver part is an INSTRUMENT GAP (receiver typing); the vocabulary part is CLAIMED; the rest is a NEW CLAIM KIND
walls.falsifier: The four-bucket partition (script/m14/cpp-w1-price.ts) closes exactly on 614,081 rows; if a future index population declares a name the partition counted as `nothing-in-the-project-declares-it`, the partition's D bucket shrinks and the W1 split is re-priced. A falsifier for the WHOLE wall: if `projectIndexDeclaration` (the task-24 claim kind) is built and verifies > 1,000 rows on the production population, this wall's D bucket becomes CLAIMED rather than a new-claim-kind request.
walls.note: The lane's own §18.9 measurement DEFERRED the task-24 claim kind on 981 sound rows over 35.6% of the wall. The four-bucket partition prices the whole wall on the production population, and it separates the CLAIMED part (the committed `iso-cpp-stdlib` vocabulary) from the part that needs a NEW claim kind.

walls.falsifier: A macro name is resolved by the PREPROCESSOR, not by a declaration — the project index deliberately does not admit macro names (charter §18.8). The falsifier: if a project-index spec were extended to record macro names as name-only declarations AND the gate resolved a call to one, this wall would become RESOLVED; until then it is ruled. The bound that would break the ruling is a corpus measurement showing a macro-defined name that the analyzer's own `#define` scan can attribute to a DEFINITION SITE — the analyzer already scans macros, so the falsifier is a mechanism, not a hope.
walls.note: 114,398 rows. The lane's own C1 measurement found 83% of the `calls` residual named a declaration in a `.h` the gate never parsed, and 3,040 of fmt's macro `#define`s were the largest single part of that. The MACRO class is the part no index can answer, because a macro is not a declaration.

walls.disposition: INSTRUMENT GAP (receiver typing) — the rows the index CAN bound but cannot choose
walls.falsifier: A member leaf whose declaring class is EXACTLY ONE in the project is decidable by a receiver fact; if a receiver-typing mechanism is built and the whole-population run shows the `exactly ONE class declares the leaf` sub-class moving out of the wall, the gap is closed. The pre-committed falsifier for the receiver-typing work was the second wave's 7,913 closure-verifiable rows, already measured and named; this wall's residual is what remains AFTER that wave.
walls.note: This is the wall the four-bucket partition's bucket C measures from the other side, and it is the largest single sub-class of it: a bare `m()` names the member without naming its class.

walls.disposition: RULED UNDECIDABLE (by construction of the type)
walls.falsifier: An `imports` edge's target is an include PATH and a `part_of` edge's target is a QUOTED include's file STEM — module endpoints either way, while the resolution key space is SYMBOLS. A file-level endpoint would have to be added to the edge model (a new relationship type or a file-claim endpoint), which is a MODEL change, not an instrument gap. The falsifier: if a file-claim endpoint existed, this wall would be decidable by a project fact (does the repo carry that path/stem?). It is RULED because the fleet's key space is symbols and no amount of indexing changes the TYPE.
walls.note: 50,915 rows on the original population. 93% of quoted includes name a real project file (the lane's I2 measurement), so the INFORMATION is there and the ENDPOINT is not. MEASURED 2026-11-17 on the reconstruction corpus: 244 `part_of` rows whose quoted stem spells a C++ keyword (`catch`, `export`, `new`, `enum`, `float`) belong on THIS wall — they were misclassified as W7 by an extension-only wall rule that treated them as keyword-spelled NAMES; a stem can be spelled like any word, and being quoted means 'part file', not 'declaration'.

walls.disposition: INSTRUMENT GAP (the index has no cross-run TYPE declarations) — the same project-fact question as W1, in type position
walls.falsifier: If the project index's `typeKinds` were extended to carry the type's DECLARING FILE (not just its name), a type-position row could be bound to the file that declares it, and this wall's `project-declares-ONCE` sub-class would move from INSTRUMENT GAP to RESOLVED. A falsifier for the ruling: a type-position row whose target the index does NOT declare and which no committed vocabulary lists is a NEW CLAIM KIND request (the same D bucket as W1's).
walls.note: The index answers 'does the project declare this NAME' — it does not answer 'which FILE declared it', so a type-position row cannot be bound to a declaration site even when the name is declared. That is the instrument's limit, measured, not assumed.

walls.disposition: INSTRUMENT GAP (the analyzer publishes LEAF names; a cpp member symbol has no distinct qualifiedName)
walls.falsifier: If the analyzer published a `qualifiedName` for cpp members, a `a::b` target would answer to a published key. The falsifier is a fixture-and-census pair: a member whose qualified name is `A::m` must be published under it, and the W4 sub-class must shrink by that count. The lane's own `isPlainIdentifier` / `buildFullName` machinery shows the shape is available — the cpp member symbol simply does not carry it.
walls.note: 2,771 rows, and it is the mirror image of the W1 wall: a name the project DOES declare, spelled in a way the key space cannot answer.

walls.disposition: RULED UNDECIDABLE (the target is the export MARKER as written)
walls.falsifier: An `exports` edge's target is the marker macro (`DART_EXPORT`, `FMT_API`), and the edge's ASSERTION is the syntactic fact that the marker appears in the declaration-specifier position. There is no declaration to bind it to — the declaration is the SOURCE of the row. A claim kind would have to claim a MACRO, which the macro ruling already refuses. The falsifier: a corpus measurement finding a case where the marker is ALSO a real declaration name in the project; that would be a separate, tiny class.

walls.disposition: RULED UNDECIDABLE (an operator spelling is not a published symbol)
walls.falsifier: The analyzer publishes members under their source spelling, and an operator's source spelling is the operator token. A published `operator==` symbol would let these rows bind — and the lane's own `friend-definition-body-owner` fixture records that publishing an `operator==` symbol CONTRADICTS an authored contract (a free-function friend definition). So the ruling is a CONTRACT conflict, and its falsifier is a Lead ruling on that conflict, not a mechanism.
walls.note: 180 rows. The one fixture failure in the lane's suite is the same contract, and it is recorded rather than overturned.
